### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/plugin-security`, touching **14** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin-cbp-read-filter.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**20** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json fb79d47cc0551615698f2931efaebd200d458450`.

⛔ **12** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin-cbp-read-filter.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **32** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json fb79d47cc0551615698f2931efaebd200d458450` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `86d2b43560537b35f5b2a9ee384c950def39940a` — the merge of head `ecf056a513b6c62c3a76d6d0d2a1b976d8688d4b` into base `fb79d47cc0551615698f2931efaebd200d458450`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 86d2b43560537b35f5b2a9ee384c950def39940a && git checkout 86d2b43560537b35f5b2a9ee384c950def39940a
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin fb79d47cc0551615698f2931efaebd200d458450 ecf056a513b6c62c3a76d6d0d2a1b976d8688d4b && git checkout -B drift-repro fb79d47cc0551615698f2931efaebd200d458450 && git merge --no-ff ecf056a513b6c62c3a76d6d0d2a1b976d8688d4b

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json fb79d47cc0551615698f2931efaebd200d458450
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs fb79d47cc0551615698f2931efaebd200d458450` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Review — FAIL

Head-sha: `2c6025c0f3c0f177e0ce5642ad48c8f1e9767149`
Reviewer: review-a (areas S1 + S3) · read 2026-11-15T13:52Z · diff read against the merge's main parent (7 files, +730/−9, matches the PR files list)
Implemented-by: session_01QsR2jVPGBoi3MCGoKbW1Hv (area S1 dispatch) · Reviewed-by: session_01QsR2jTjrNnh6b2BkCXFugM
Ruling reviewed against: 6893666857 (replaces 6893097935)

**What holds**

- The read side matches the ruling, point by point. Step 5 drops only a leaf that is the whole `$in` comparand on the REQUIRED `master_detail` field of a `controlled_by_parent` object, in an AND position (the node itself or `$and` members, never `$or`/`$not`, never a merged-key position). Both conditions are needed: the master's answered scope is `undefined`, and the caller holds `viewAllRecords`/`modifyAllRecords` on the object that node scopes. A nested scope emptied by its own drops answers `undefined`, so the chain drops whole only when every hop is unrestricted and the caller holds View All on each detail on the way. A restricted hop keeps its leaf and everything below it.
- Fail-closed paths keep the chain. These are a delegated caller, a service without the member, and a service that throws. `ReadableIdsChain.operation` is typed to the four read verbs, so no write verb composes through step 5 directly.
- The tenant wall stays out of the dropped leaf. A walled tenant admin's master scope carries the tenant equality, so it is not `undefined`, and pin (e) measures that.
- Pins (b), (c) and (d) are the ruling's reverse pins, and the ablation table shows each red under the mutation that should redden it. `engine.ts` is the approved 2-line getter widening inside the host literal.
- Changeset: patch, `Clause-②: no` / `Metadata-protocol: none` as claimed, and the ruling's release-note sentence is there. The "do not land before #33820" line is in the PR body.

**Must-fix**

1. **The drop reaches the write doors, and nothing rules, declares or pins that.** Three security-plugin checks ask the read door with the caller's own context, and for this reader class that door now returns orphan rows:
   - the predicate-write narrowing (`readableRowsScopeForPredicateWrite`, `ql.find`);
   - the 2.8 gate's predicate leg (`controlledByParentPredicateWriteMasters`, `ql.find`);
   - the by-id read check at step 2.7 (`callerCannotReadAddressedRow` → `getCallerPreImage` → `ql.findOne`).

   Read from the code at this head (not run here), here is what follows for a View All reader over unrestricted hops:
   - A predicate `update`/`delete` whose predicate matches a row with an empty REQUIRED master is now refused whole. `controlledByParentPredicateWriteMasters` throws `MasterReferenceMissingError` (422) for any such row among the readable ids. On main that row was not readable, so the same write succeeded on the other rows. An admin's filtered mass update or delete on a detail object can now fail because of one orphan it matches. A request that was accepted is refused, which is a narrowing on exactly the reader class this PR targets.
   - A predicate write that matches a dangling-FK row now sends a master id that does not exist into the master-edit walk. Whichever way that walk answers, it is a write-side answer the ruling did not make.
   - A by-id `update`/`delete` of an orphan now gets past step 2.7, so it no longer answers 404. It reaches the 2.8 stored-row legs instead.

   Ruling 6893666857 is a read ruling: "that reader **sees** null and dangling-FK rows". The changeset says the same. Pick one of these:
   - **(a) Preferred, and it keeps `Clause-②: no` honest:** leave the write doors byte-identical. The reads those three checks make on behalf of a write keep the chain. Add pins where the View All admin runs a predicate `delete` and a predicate `update` over a set that includes an empty-required-master orphan: both still succeed on the other rows and leave the orphan alone. Add one by-id pin that still answers 404. Ablate the mechanism. Each of these pins should go red on the current head, which also measures this finding.
   - **(b)** Take the write-side consequence to the seat as a ruling. If it is accepted, declare it: the predicate-write refusal is a `(narrowing)` arm with its `!`, BREAKING note, ADR-0087 disposition and battery, and the review face moves to `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`. Pin it either way.

   Either route needs a claim amendment, because the fix or the pins sit in `plugin-security` write-door files outside the current surface.

**Should-fix**

2. The `computeControlledByParentFilter` docblock in `security-plugin.ts` (the "driver compiles the composed leaf as `masterFK IN (SELECT …)`" contract text) is the method's contract, and this PR changes what that sentence promises for one reader class. Fold a prose-only paragraph pointing at step 5 into the same claim amendment as item 1. Then the contract text and the new behaviour land together, and the seat carries nothing.

**Nits (no re-review needed)**

3. `readerViewsAllOf` calls `getEffectiveObjectPermissions` on every read where some master answers unrestricted, which includes plain-member reads over a public master (pin (d)). The result is cached per read only. That is fine at today's cost; note it if the service call grows.
4. #33652 conflicts with this PR as text in the same function. The PR body's analysis (no conflict in meaning, because its semi-join leaves never enter `chain.answers`) is accepted. Whichever lands second rebases, and I delta-review that rebase.

**Gates:** not judged. At review time 16 check-runs were in progress, 16 success, 16 skipped, none red. Landing also waits on #33820 per the ruling, even after a PASS.

Next: a new head with item 1 (route a or b) and item 2. I review the delta only.

## Review — PASS (delta)

Head-sha: `df3fb3b9ad5558a2e9ebf205e12ac0fbd4499fe1`
Reviewer: review-a (areas S1 + S3) · read 2026-11-15T17:15Z · delta `2c6025c0..df3fb3b9`: `2fadb3d3` (code), `8d9c38be` (pins), `f72049d6` (docblock), `d3fce3c6` (changeset), plus two clean main merges that touch none of this PR's files
Implemented-by: session_01QsR2jVPGBoi3MCGoKbW1Hv (area S1 dispatch) · Reviewed-by: session_01QsR2jTjrNnh6b2BkCXFugM
Prior verdict: FAIL 6895328067 (must-fix 1, should-fix 2) · delta report 6897525187 · route (a), claim amendment 6895620230

**Must-fix 1 (write doors): fixed, by route (a).**

- `executeWithMiddleware` runs a write's middleware chain inside `READABLE_IDS_WRITE_IN_FLIGHT` (an `AsyncLocalStorage`). `readerViewsAllOf` answers "no View All" inside that scope, so step 5 drops nothing for any read made on a write's behalf. That covers the predicate-write narrowing, the 2.8 predicate leg, the step-2.7 by-id read and a hook's read.
- **Coverage.** The scope keys on `isWriteEpochOperation`, which is `insert`, `update`, `delete`, `purge` and `restore`. Those are the operation names every write caller of `executeWithMiddleware` sets (`engine-insert`, `engine-update`, `engine-delete-and-aggregate` with `permanent ? 'purge' : 'delete'`, `recycle-bin/purge`, `recycle-bin/restore`). A nested read inherits the store, because its own `executeWithMiddleware` call takes the `else` branch without clearing it.
- **Fails closed.** Wherever the scope reaches, it can only restore the pre-ruling answer. So a read that outlives or escapes the write and still sees the store keeps the chain, which is what every reader had before. No plugin-security write-door source changed, so the write doors are byte-identical to main, and `Clause-②: no` / `Metadata-protocol: none` hold again.
- **Pins** are outside-in on the real rig. A predicate delete and a predicate update over sets holding empty-master and dangling-master orphans land on the other rows and leave the orphans. By-id update and delete of an orphan still answer `RECORD_NOT_FOUND`/404. A hook read inside a write sees no orphan, while the same reader's plain read, outside the write, does. I accept the reported measurements: each pin is red on `2c6025c0` with the failure the FAIL predicted (422 refusal, 403 instead of 404, the hook seeing the orphans), and both ablations (the store guard, and the scope wrapper) turn 4/4 red.

**Should-fix 2: fixed.** The `computeControlledByParentFilter` docblock now names the reader class step 5 serves and says the drop is read-only and that this method still writes the leaf for every caller. The changeset adds the "writes are unchanged" paragraph. Both are true of the code at this head.

**Nits (no re-review needed)**

1. `READABLE_IDS_WRITE_IN_FLIGHT` is exported from the formula module for its one engine importer. If `objectql`'s index ever re-exports that module wholesale, keep this symbol out of the public surface.
2. Earlier nits 3 and 4 stand: the per-read `getEffectiveObjectPermissions` cost, and the known text conflict with #33652 (2 hunks in the same file). Whichever PR lands second rebases, and I delta-review that rebase.

**Gates:** at review time 37 success, 18 skipped, none red, so every check is green.

**Landing precondition:** the ruling requires #33820 to land first. At review time #33820 is closed (completed). Confirm that its ADR-0139 status line is on main before arming.

> `↳ 失败原因` 是判读的关键：**超时**（`Test timed out in …` / `Hook timed out in …`）多半是负载/时序，不是本 PR 的回归；
> **断言**（`AssertionError: …`）才指向真实的行为改变。两者的 `FAIL` 行长得一模一样，只有这一行能区分。
>
> ⚠️ **断言这一侧有一类例外，判据是断言在测什么，不是它是不是 `AssertionError`。** 断言的对象是**产品行为**（一个值、一个形状、一次拒收）⇒ 照上面读：真实的行为改变，去查，⛔ 不要重排掉；
> 断言的对象是**这次实验自身的有效性前提**（跑完的耗时、负载下的先后、任何只在时间预算内才成立的条件）⇒ 它跟**超时**是同一类，同样对负载敏感，重排一次是合法的判别手段。
> 识别是机械的：断言的消息或它比较的值本身点名了一段**时长、一个时间戳、一个耗时计数**。实测过的一对 —— `AssertionError: SecurityPlugin.init() ran: expected false to be true` 测的是产品行为（真回归）；
> `AssertionError: this run took over a second, so second-precision stamps could have differed too: expected 1006 to be less than 1000` 测的是实验前提：它守护的那条不变式当时是绿的，同一个 head 原样重排一次即成功。
> 穿着 `AssertionError` 外衣的时间测量，仍然是时间测量。（⛔ 这只改「怎么读一次红」，不改「哪些测试可以重排」——后者由别处管。）
